query:
The group moved toward a scan-sharing arrangement so absent members could participate in critiques. What did one member's response in that moment reveal about their actual position, and what specifically in how they responded tells you that?

Options:
A. Margot
B. Yuki
C. Otto
D. Fen
context:
[1] (about=Margot, episodic, t2 @2025-02-08T10:20:00) I see.
[2] (about=Otto, episodic, t2 @2025-02-08T10:18:00) I will say what needs saying. Scanning is a compromise. The tonal range in a wet print does not survive digitisation cleanly. In my experience, the print is the work. I would rather members attended. That said, I understand the practical argument.
[3] (about=Bex, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Fully supports scan-sharing; thinks it would make group more connected between sessions.
[4] (about=Bex, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Asks for explanation of scanning settings: bit depth, colour profile, greyscale vs RGB for black and white prints.
[5] (about=Callum, profile, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Otto will have thoughts on scanning.
[6] (about=Callum, core, t12 @2025-03-15T10:04:00) Best collaborative experience; Fen kept him honest about editorial line.
[7] (about=Fen, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Supports scan-sharing; would have helped last month.
[8] (about=Fen, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Appreciated scans; grain read well enough to critique the two frames most uncertain about.
[9] (about=Margot, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Accepts scan-sharing as a practical necessity for absent members, not as a general practice.
[10] (about=Margot, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00, [earlier-state]) Accepts scan-sharing trial.
[11] (about=Margot, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Accepts scan-sharing trial as a practical necessity for absent members, not as a general practice.
[12] (about=Nora, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Proposes scan-sharing trial for absent members; anyone who prints also produces a scan at 2400 dpi minimum.
[13] (about=Otto, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Scanning is a compromise; tonal range of wet print does not digitise cleanly; print is the work; prefers attendance but understands practical argument.
[14] (about=Otto, core, t12 @2025-03-15T10:04:00) Documentary collaboration requires clearly agreed division of editorial authority; aesthetic disagreements manageable but curatorial disagreements not.
[15] (about=Priya, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Scan resolution affects readability of fine detail; worth agreeing a minimum standard per print type rather than a single number.
[16] (about=Priya, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Scan resolution must be sufficient for critique; under 2400 dpi loses grain detail.
[17] (about=Sol, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Thinks scan-sharing is a great idea; would have helped when missed November session; can help with scanning settings.
[18] (about=Sol, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Scan-sharing means can show process mid-project rather than waiting for session; changes how group works.
[19] (about=Yuki, core, t10 @2025-03-08T10:05:00) Scan resolution should be agreed per print rather than set as a blanket standard; grain structure does not hold cleanly above 2400.
[20] (about=Yuki, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) Practical case is clear; question is about what we consider primary object of critique.
agent_answer:
C. **Otto**

Otto's response at that moment revealed that his **actual position was reluctant acceptance, not genuine endorsement**: he saw scan-sharing as a compromise, believed "the print is the work," and would rather members attended in person — he only came along because he understood the practical argument.

The specifics in how he responded tell you this:

- He opened with **"I will say what needs saying"** — signaling he felt compelled to voice a dissenting or uncomfortable view rather than simply celebrating the arrangement.
- His substantive claim — **"The tonal range in a wet print does not survive digitisation cleanly. In my experience, the print is the work"** — shows his real aesthetic commitment to the physical print over the scan.
- The concession clause **"That said, I understand the practical argument"** reveals that his agreement was an acknowledgement of necessity, not a change of heart — he accepted the scan-sharing scheme while making it clear he would prefer live attendance.
